subject: Audit trail & integrity confirmation — PagerFlow incident follow-up
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: initial log sweep — PagerFlow incident (REDWOOD-2104)

Hi team,

Quick internal update from the ops sweep I ran this morning against the timeframe 2026-02-23 22:00 -> 2026-02-24 04:00 PST for incident REDWOOD-2104. High level: no anomalous outbound transfers detected, and authentication events look consistent with expected service accounts.

What I checked:
- VPC flow logs (aggregated) — no sustained high-volume egress to unknown hosts; all external flows correlate to known vendor IPs.
- Object store access (s3) — reads/writes during window from service roles only; no mass list/endpoint patterns.
- API audit logs — no unusual token issuances or long-lived token creation.
- KV cache integrity — checksum snapshots line up across replicas; no missing keys in the snapshot sequence.

Attached: ops-log-20260224-snippet.txt (filtered lines), s3-connection-summary-20260224.csv (connection counts by destination).

Caveats: the sweep is an initial operational review, not a formal attestation. If PagerFlow security needs additional artifacts (TLS handshakes, raw packet captures, or object-store GET headers), let me know and I can pull them for the requested window.

-Marcus
Marcus Lin
Site Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>

Subject: Request: audit trail & integrity confirmation for recent PagerFlow outage (forwarded findings)

Samantha,

Following up on the PagerFlow outage last night — we're sending you an internal summary of the checks we ran and asking whether your team can confirm any customer-visible data integrity impacts on your side. We want to get a mutual statement for each of our joint customers.

Forwarded below is the ops sweep from Marcus. The short ask: can your security team (1) review the attached summary, (2) run a complimentary check against your ingress/e2e logs for the same window, and (3) provide a short confirmation note (or a requested list of additional artifacts) so we can close the loop with impacted customers?

I've attached a one-page ops summary for PagerFlow security to review (redwood-ops-summary-20260224.pdf). If you prefer a quick call (15 min), we're available 2:30 or 3:00 PT today.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan

Subject: Re: Request: audit trail & integrity confirmation for recent PagerFlow outage (forwarded findings)

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the summary and for flagging this promptly. Our SOC team has done an initial correlation for the same timeframe. Preliminary notes:
- On our ingest tier, we do not see any bulk export activity or anomalous consumer-side requests originating from PagerFlow-managed agents.
- We do see a small number of retries from token refreshes that line up with the outage window; those are being triaged as service-level errors rather than auth compromises.

We'd like to request the following artifacts to complete our attestation:
- Raw TLS handshake timeseries for affected edge nodes (to correlate latency spikes)
- Object-store pre-signed URL access logs (if available) for 2026-02-23 22:00 -> 2026-02-24 04:00 PST
- The listing of external IPs in the s3-connection-summary CSV with associated hostname resolution (if you have that).

I've looped in security@pagerflow.com; we'll aim to provide a short attestation once we complete those checks. If you can share the requested artifacts, we'll prioritize it and respond with a signed confirmation note.

Best,
Samantha Ortiz
Director, Infrastructure Security | PagerFlow
samantha@pagerflow.com

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha@pagerflow.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 16:37:00 -08:00
Subject: Redwoods' compiled attestation & artifacts for PagerFlow (INC-2104)

Samantha / PagerFlow Security,

Attached: redwood-integrity-attestation-20260225.pdf (signed) and the requested supporting artifacts. Summary of checks completed by the Redwood security/ops teams for window 2026-02-23 22:00 -> 2026-02-24 04:00 PST:

1) VPC flow aggregate analysis — compared per-node egress volume to baseline (last 30 days). Result: no statistically significant outbound spike outside of scheduled vendor traffic.
2) Object-store access patterns — enumerated PUT/GET/DELETE operations, verified object counts and checksums against the snapshot taken at 02:10 PST. No bulk listing or mass download patterns observed.
3) API audit: token issuance and revocation graphs show normal rates; no long-lived tokens created outside of regular service roles.
4) KV store snapshots — sequence numbers match and checksum validation passed across replicas; no missing ranges.
5) Endpoint auth logs & TLS handshake samples — provided in attached tar (tls-handshakes-sample.tgz) for your team to correlate.

We are providing the artifacts you requested (TLS handshake samples, presigned-url access logs, and expanded s3 connection hostnames). The attestation document outlines the methodology and indicates that our analysis found no evidence of data exfiltration from Redwood-managed systems for the requested window. That language is intentionally scoped to our environment and the time window; for a mutual customer-facing statement we can coordinate phrasing with your legal/compliance teams.

If you'd like us to redact any hostnames or share a joint attestation template, we're happy to collaborate.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Security Operations | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com

Attachments in this message: redwood-integrity-attestation-20260225.pdf, tls-handshakes-sample.tgz, presigned-url-access-logs-20260224.csv
